necessary_context.content: Input A in R^{n x d}, epsilon in (0,1), rank k <= n,d; Gaussian Pi in R^{d x k}; q=Theta(log(d)/sqrt(epsilon)); K=[A Pi,(AA^T)A Pi,...,(AA^T)^q A Pi]. Orthonormalize K, form M=Q^T AA^T Q, select its top k singular vectors Ubar_k and return Z=Q Ubar_k. The displayed Q dimension n x qk conflicts with the q+1 displayed blocks; no rank-deficient completion is specified in this algorithm box.
necessary_context.name: Algorithm 2 input and output

necessary_context.content: Theorem 1 states Algorithm 2 requires O(log(d)/sqrt(epsilon)) iterations and O(nnz(A) k q) runtime excluding lower-order terms. It points to Theorems 6 and 7 for runtime and Theorems 10–12 for accuracy. These runtime proofs were not read in this extraction.
necessary_context.name: Main result resource scope

necessary_context.content: A_l is a best rank-l approximation. For orthonormal Z and its first l columns Z_l, Definition 8 gives E(Z_l,A)=||A_l||_F^2-||Z_l Z_l^T A||_F^2. Section 6.1 assumes k <= rank(A) for simplicity and asserts applicability beyond that case without specifying a completion procedure here. Lemma 9 Property 1 uses m=count{i:sigma_i >= (1+epsilon/2)sigma_{k+1}} and bounds E(Z_l,A) by (epsilon/2)sigma_{k+1}^2 for l <= m. Its proof opening uses q >= c log(d/epsilon)/sqrt(epsilon), then invokes 1/epsilon=O(poly(d)) or a classical partial-SVD fallback.
necessary_context.locator: PDF p.10, section 6.1, Definition 8, Lemma 9 and proof opening
necessary_context.name: Approximation notation and standing assumption

necessary_context.content: Theorem 10 states that Algorithms 1 and 2 return Z with probability 99/100 satisfying ||A-ZZ^T A||_2 <= (1+epsilon)||A-A_k||_2. Its proof uses Lemma 9 Property 1, the Frobenius-to-spectral implication attributed to Theorem 3.4 of reference [22] and reproduced as Lemma 15, and Lemma 3 for projection monotonicity. Those dependency proofs have not been fully read here. Equation (13) and the displayed final projection identity require further mathematical checking before extracting a reference Theorem.
